items.title: National Assembly, Senate pass resolutions endorsing Centre's imposition of emergency in KP
items.description:
ISLAMABAD: Shortly after the National Assembly passed a resolution endorsing the federal government’s imposition of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Wednesday, the Senate also gave its approval for the measure.
The Centre had imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP on Sunday, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The move followed weeks of political tensions between the Centre and the PTI after the latter announced a long march to Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan.

items.title: Lagging behind
items.description:
THE IMF’s latest World Economic Outlook projects Pakistan’s economy to grow by 3.5pc in the current fiscal year, while average inflation climbs to 9.9pc. The current account is expected to slip into a deficit of 1pc of GDP. This forecast points to an economy that remains vulnerable despite recent gains in macroeconomic stability.
The economy expanded by 3.6pc last year. Further slowdown matters for a country with a rapidly increasing population, entrenched poverty, and high unemployment. Growth at this pace will hardly raise incomes meaningfully or absorb new entrants into the labour market.
